questions.q: Which DMV reports tempdb space usage broken down by user objects, internal objects, and the version store?
options: sys.dm_db_file_space_usage
sys.dm_exec_requests
sys.dm_os_wait_stats
sys.database_files
questions.explain: sys.dm_db_file_space_usage, queried against tempdb, splits current allocation into exactly those three categories.

questions.q: What does the version store in tempdb actually hold?
options: Old row versions kept for snapshot isolation or read-committed snapshot isolation
The compiled execution plans for recently run queries
A backup copy of every user database's schema
Index fragmentation statistics
questions.explain: Row versioning for snapshot-based isolation levels stores old versions in tempdb's version store until they're no longer needed.

questions.q: How do you identify which specific session is consuming the most tempdb space right now?
options: Query sys.dm_db_session_space_usage and rank by allocated-minus-deallocated page counts
Query sys.database_files and look at the max_size column
There is no way to attribute tempdb usage to a specific session
Query sys.dm_os_wait_stats filtered to WRITELOG waits
questions.explain: sys.dm_db_session_space_usage attributes tempdb page allocations to the session that made them.

questions.q: In a sys.database_files space query, why divide size and FILEPROPERTY(name, 'SpaceUsed') by 128?
options: Both values are stored in 8 KB pages, and 128 pages of 8 KB equal 1 MB
128 is the maximum number of data files SQL Server allows per database
It converts rows into a percentage automatically
SQL Server requires all space calculations to be divided by 128
questions.explain: 8 KB per page times 128 pages equals 1,024 KB, i.e. 1 MB — the standard page-to-megabyte conversion.

questions.q: A tempdb space report shows version_store_mb far larger than user_objects_mb or internal_objects_mb. What does that usually point to?
options: A long-running transaction under snapshot isolation preventing old row versions from being cleaned up
A missing index on a frequently queried table
Excessive use of temp tables by application code
The tempdb data file has autogrowth disabled
questions.explain: The version store can't clean up row versions still needed by an open snapshot transaction, so it grows unbounded until that transaction ends.
